newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon bombs kill two militiamen, two civilians.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon bombs kill two militiamen, two civilians.

text.p: Two pro-Israeli militiamen were killed in a roadside bomb explosion in south Lebanon on Wednesday hours after two civilians died in another blast, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
They said the blast occurred as a car carrying the two militiamen traveled along the road from the village of Bkassine to the town of Jizzine.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsibility for the attack.
Jizzine is a strip of territory officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under the control of the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia.
One of the blast victims, Claude Khalil, was a member of the SLA security forces and the other, Nimr Nammour, belonged to the SLA police force, the sources said.
The attack was the third bombing in the same area on Wednesday. Two civilians were killed and one policeman and one civilian were wounded in two separate roadside bomb attacks earlier in the day.
After the first two bombings, Israeli warplanes rocketed suspected pro-Iranian Hizbollah targets in Lebanon's Syrian-controlled eastern Bekaa valley, security sources said.
There was no immediate word about casualties in the air raid.
Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops and their local militia allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
